solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Want to hold fool back when keeping dry

indicators.note: the first word grips the next one, holding it inside itself
going back means the word for a fool is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: want in the sense of lack, an absence
a nit is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.surface: Someone longs to keep a fool in check while staying off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as desire, but here it means lack, as in 'for want of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying off alcohol is called abstinence, and a 'dry' person or household is teetotal.

clue.text: Attack from male hiding in a thicket

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written
a bush is a thicket of shrubs

explanation.surface: A man springs out of a thicket in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes into A BUSH, between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from a concealed position.

clue.text: Catchphrase is a big hit primarily before end of election

indicators.note: this puts the hit first in line, ahead of the article that precedes it in the clue
only the final letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: a slog is a big swipe in cricket
taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A campaign slogan proves a big hit just before polling day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is politics, and a slogan is exactly what wins an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase, as used in advertising or campaigning.

clue.text: Southern Asian class briefly tours a north American city

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: India is in South Asia
taken as written
class in the sense of refinement or polish

explanation.surface: A South Asian class goes on a tour of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' in the sense of refinement is polish. 'Tours' does no work in the wordplay and reads as a loose join; the pieces follow the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Indianapolis is the state capital of Indiana in the north of the United States.

clue.text: Forgetting starter warms a meal

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun meaning food, standing for a meal

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter, and forgetting it means leaving it off

blocks.note: to heat is to warm

explanation.surface: Someone skips the starter and heats up a main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' sounds like a first course, but here it is the first letter of HEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, the stuff of a meal.

clue.text: Happy sister carried uniform

indicators.note: what is carried is held within, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: content means happy
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A cheerful sister wore her uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing, but it is the adjective meaning unvarying.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistent means unchanging and even, which is what uniform means as an adjective.

clue.text: Some twitcher hears ostrich-like bird

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher hears a large flightless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: It sits across twitcHER HEArs. A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, a ratite related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Warning device has to emit light in tree

blocks.note: a car horn sounds a warning
to beam is to shine

explanation.surface: A warning device must flash a light from inside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a hardwood tree of the birch family, often used for hedging.

clue.text: … is what it will be if the typist doesn't get a shift on

definitions.text: … is what it will be if the typist doesn't get a shift on

blocks.clueFragment: if the typist doesn't get a shift on
blocks.note: surface reading: an idle typist who needs to hurry up
setter's reading: the clue's own number is eight, and the eight key pressed with the shift key gives a star symbol

explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis stands for the clue number, 8. On a standard keyboard, Shift+8 types the star symbol, so a typist using the shift key turns the 8 into that symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped printing symbol, which sits above the 8 on a keyboard.

clue.text: Mineral found in veins?

blocks.note: surface reading: a mineral that occurs in seams, or veins, of rock
setter's reading: the veins of the body, where blood runs, so a stone made of blood

explanation.walkthrough: Mineral veins are ordinary geology; the question mark invites the blood vessels instead, giving a stone named after blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodstone is a green chalcedony gemstone flecked with red spots of jasper.

clue.text: Flipping time machine is missing—blast!

indicators.note: the two letters of the word 'is' are absent from the machine's name
flipping something over turns it end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the TARDIS is Doctor Who's time machine

explanation.surface: Someone has lost their time machine and swears about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse to match 'blast', but it turns TARD round once IS has gone from TARDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance, interchangeable as expletives.

clue.text: In broadcast Dylan wails I'm an old singer

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Bob Dylan, singing on air, laments being past it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan suggests Bob Dylan, but he is only fodder for another singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Williams was an American crooner, famous for Moon River, who died in 2012.

clue.text: Son on horse crushing head of Colorado beetle

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the son sitting on the horse squeezes another letter between himself and it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the first letter of the state's name
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A boy on horseback crushes a Colorado beetle, a notorious potato pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colorado beetle' reads as one pest, but the beetle is the definition and Colorado only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt and a common motif on amulets.

clue.text: Red jag, say, outside pub with a blonde in the front

indicators.note: one word wraps round the outside of the rest
only the letter at the very front of that word is used

blocks.note: a Jag (Jaguar) is an example of a car
an inn is a pub
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A red Jaguar parked outside a pub with a blonde sitting in the front seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the front' seems to seat the blonde in the car, but it selects the word's first letter. Jag is the everyday British name for a Jaguar car.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a bright scarlet mercury ore, and its name is used for the vermilion colour it gives.

clue.text: More than one joker restricts King being played

indicators.note: something being played is performed freely, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: In a card game, multiple jokers limit what the king can do.
explanation.walkthrough: Joker, King and played all suggest cards, but the joker is the definition, a prankster.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is someone who plays tricks, so more than one is a group of pranksters.

clue.text: Many consider Honister to be such a difficult place to be

definitions.text: Many consider Honister to be such

blocks.clueFragment: Many consider Honister to be such
blocks.note: first meaning: Honister is a scenic mountain pass in England's Lake District, so a literal attractive pass
second meaning: the idiom for an awkward or sorry state of affairs

explanation.surface: Honister, admired by many, is also a hard spot to find yourself in.
explanation.walkthrough: Honister Pass is a steep, scenic road through the Lake District hills in Cumbria; the phrase is taken literally there and idiomatically after.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'things have come to a pretty pass' describes a bad or difficult situation.

clue.text: Artist portraying small vessel going around lake on hill

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cup is a drinking vessel
L is the abbreviation for lake
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A painter depicts a little boat circling a lake below a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, matching the lake, but it is a drinking vessel; in a down clue 'on' lets the hill sit last.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor is an artist who makes three-dimensional works in stone, metal or clay.

clue.text: There's some white in this paint

definitions.note: a cryptic definition: the shell is what holds an egg's white

blocks.note: first meaning: the casing of an egg, which holds the egg white
second meaning: a paint with a low-sheen finish

explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, it sounds like a paint tinted with white; split it, and the white is egg white inside the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a low-sheen paint finish named after the surface of an egg, and an egg's shell encloses its white.

clue.text: Informed experts caught in dreadful congestion

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Experts in the know get stuck in an awful traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: The C is caught up in the jumble along with the letters of congestion.
explanation.definitionFit: The cognoscenti are people with expert knowledge of a subject, connoisseurs in the know.

clue.text: It's awkward being left in Paris

blocks.note: first meaning: socially clumsy
second meaning: the French word for left

explanation.surface: Being abandoned in Paris is an uncomfortable situation.
explanation.definitionFit: English borrowed the French word for left-handed to mean socially clumsy or tactless.

clue.text: Odd number of players performing for 30 days on film

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so comes first

blocks.note: September has 30 days, and Sept is its short form
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A band plays for a month on a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd number' hints at strange music, but seven is simply an odd number.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a group of seven musicians, and seven is an odd number.

clue.text: Most passionate lutists played with energy

indicators.note: playing with something rearranges it, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The most ardent lute players performed with great vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustiest is the superlative of lusty, full of vigour and sexual desire.

clue.text: Crack cocaine set out

blocks.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
to set out is to leave

explanation.surface: Crack cocaine is laid out on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack cocaine' reads as one drug; crack is the definition, a verb meaning split.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split something apart, as a crack does.

clue.text: American woman who once won Wimbledon

definitions.note: the definition picks out a person, the tennis player

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A female American tennis player was once a Wimbledon champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a woman champion, but the winner is a man: Arthur Ashe, Wimbledon champion in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe, the American tennis player, won the Wimbledon men's singles title in 1975.

clue.text: Layer toiletry oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A layer of some toiletry looks strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of stacked rows or levels, as in a wedding cake.

clue.text: Practise with an awkward animal

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsily arranged, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to rehearse with a clumsy pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian is a long-haired breed of domestic cat, so a specific kind of animal.

clue.text: Turn over a bun

blocks.note: first meaning: to rotate, as a ball moves along the ground
second meaning: a small loaf of bread for one person

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests flipping a bun; the clue splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for revolving and a noun for a small individual bread bun.

clue.text: Valuation of corrupt men's assets

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoiled and changed from its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An appraisal of what crooked men own.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation, as when property is assessed for its worth.
